text:
In regular expressions, `^` and `$` are **anchors**. They do not match actual characters; instead, they match a **position** relative to the string or line.

### `^` The Caret (Start Anchor)
The `^` symbol matches the position at the very beginning of the string.

*   **Pattern:** `^Apple`
*   **Matches:** "**Apple** pie", "**Apple**"
*   **Does not match:** "Green Apple" (because "Apple" is not at the start).

### `$` The Dollar Sign (End Anchor)
The `$` symbol matches the position at the very end of the string.

*   **Pattern:** `pie$`
*   **Matches:** "Apple **pie**", "Apple**pie**"
*   **Does not match:** "piece of cake" (because "pie" is not at the end).

---

### Combined: Exact Matching
When you use both `^` and `$` together, you ensure the pattern matches the **entire** string from start to finish, with no extra characters allowed.

| Pattern | String | Result | Reason |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `cat` | "catapult" | Match | "cat" exists inside the string. |
| `^cat$` | "catapult" | No Match | The string contains more than just "cat". |
| `^cat$` | "cat" | **Match** | The string starts and ends exactly with "cat". |

### Multiline Mode
By default, these anchors treat the entire input as one single string. However, if you enable **Multiline Mode** (usually the `/m` flag):
*   `^` matches the start of the string **and** the start of every new line (`\n`).
*   `$` matches the end of the string **and** the end of every line.

### Summary Table
| Symbol | Meaning | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `^` | Start of string | `^Hello` matches "Hello world" |
| `$` | End of string | `world$` matches "Hello world" |
| `^...$` | Exact match | `^abc$` matches "abc" only |
